steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Lightly grease a 9x5-inch loaf pan.

Break up apples in filling in a medium bowl using a potato masher; set aside. Cream butter, white sugar, and brown sugar together in a large bowl; stir in apple filling, eggs, and vanilla extract until well blended. Sift flour, baking soda, cinnamon, and salt together in a separate bowl; stir into apple mixture, then stir in raisins and walnuts. Pour batter into the prepared pan.
Bake in the preheated oven until a toothpick inserted into center of loaf comes out clean, about 1 hour. Cool in the pan for 15 minutes, then turn out onto a wire rack to cool completely.

raw_recipe.headline: Quick Apple Pie Bread
raw_recipe.description: Take a recipe shortcut and use prepared apple pie filling in this cinnamon- and vanilla-enhanced quick apple pie bread loaded with raisins and walnuts.

review.reviewBody: very yummy bread. I found though that I had to put some of the batter into another pan because it was more than my bread pan would hold. I will for sure be making this again!

I divided the batter into 7 mini loaves and baked them for 40 minutes and they turned out perfect. Really good recipe. Moist and tender and very tasty. If things are not getting done, check your oven temp. It's not really bread, it's cake. Really good 'cake'.

I used a 9 x 13 metal pan and baked it for 30 minutes. Turned out moist and delicious. The next time I make this -- and I'll definitely be making this again--- I would add a cup of chopped apple pieces. That was the only complaint....everyone wanted more apple inside. This is more of a cake than a bread. I did add a cinnamon glaze on top which I will do again. Love this!

Great recipe. I used a Bundt pan. I only used a 1\2can of pie filling. I used 8T butter. I added 1cup mashed bananas to compensate for the reduction in pie filling. (I had a half can left from another recipe and wanted to try this recipe so I improvised ) baking time in Bundt pan was 45minutes
Didn't do nuts and raisins and had a 15 ounce can of pie filling, so used half cup of applesauce and did 1/4 teaspoon of nutmeg and ginger also.

This is now on my list of family favorites. Very easy to follow recipe and great flavor. It's a tiny bit too sweet to me, probably because of the apple filling. Next time I will lessen the sugars to 1/3 or 1/4 cup. I used "Infibra" bread flour instead of all purpose flour, which gives it a better texture and taste for our liking. Also, increases it's nutritional value and fiber. I highly recommend giving this recipe a try💕!
I puréed my home canned apple pie filling, and put in muffin tin. Turned out great.

Made this 2 days ago and it's gone now. I split the dough into 2. One loaf had no add-ins and I used pumpkin pie spice instead of just cinnamon. A very nice quick bread. The other loaf (as pictured) had dried cranberries, ground pecans and a quick streusel topping. This was much more like a special cake/dessert. Both were moist after 60 minutes in the oven.

Next time I will either use 2.5 cups of flour or 2 cups of bread flour to get a slightly stiffer bread to slice and toast. I did put a slice of the bread that is pictured in the toaster but the apple to bread ratio didn't allow it to really toast up. It was simply warmed from the toaster but not sturdy enough to put some butter on. If that makes sense?

I just tried this recipe (i noticed the other reviews were fr 10 years ago) and followed it exactly, except, I baked it in a 9 x 13 pan (as the other reviewer said) and baked it for 35 minutes. I turned out good and moist.
I also drizzled it with cinnamon glaze and it was a perfect bread for fall.
My son loved it so much!!!
I used a longer bundt loaf pan, it fit just fine. Taking to rosary group. Sprinkled with confectioners sugar

I have made this many times in both loaf and muffins for my DIL’s coffee shop. I always use the suggestion to add more apple. I usually add 2 apples finely chopped. I also use pumpkin pie spice because I like it. It’s a keeper!!
Everyone loved the breads. I do them in mini loaf pans to give to friends and family. Everyone loved them so much they are going into our holiday baskets this year

Had a can of apple pie filling I really needed to use up, and got a new favorite recipe!! We used a bigger metal loaf pan-the kind you use for bread loaves, and it came out perfect!! It was super moist and delicious and a big hit with the entire family. We did omit the raisins and walnuts, and used margarine instead of butter, otherwise no changes were made.
I baked mine in 4 mini loaf pans. The batter did not spill over. Tasty bread but I did have my doubts about the raisins. Next time I will leave them out. Thank you for sharing your recipe.

Good recipe. I didn't have 21 oz can of apple pie filling in my pantry, but I did have a 14 oz can of cooked apples. This may have made it a slight heaver than the original recipe, but it was still very good. I also added about 1/4 cup of sour cream. I'll make it again. My husband loved it.
